title: URL Rewriting: Redirect and Rewrite Requests

steps.text: Old addresses keep arriving long after a page has been renamed. The URL Rewriting feature redirects or rewrites incoming requests, so visitors reach the right content. In this video, you create a redirect rule and a rewrite rule, test both, and manage the list.
A page is renamed, but its old address stays in bookmarks, search results, and links on other sites. A folder of files moves, and pages keep pointing to the old location.
A Redirect rule sends the visitor to another address, so the address in the browser changes. Use it when a page is renamed or moved, so that old links and bookmarks keep working.
A Rewrite rule answers with the content of another address, and the address in the browser stays the same. Use it to serve content from a location the visitor never sees.
Rules are kept in a list and checked from the top down. A Rewrite rule can stop the rules below it from running. Addresses under the admin prefix, which is /Admin by default, are always left alone.

A rule matches addresses with a pattern, written as a regular expression. A caret marks the start of an address, and a dollar sign marks its end. Parentheses capture text, and $1 in the substitution puts the captured text back.
In the admin menu, choose Tools, then Features. The list holds the features of the site, so search for URL Rewriting.
Select Enable on the URL Rewriting row. A message confirms it: The feature URL Rewriting was enabled.
With the feature enabled, the Tools menu has a URL Rewriting item. Users see it when their role has the Manage URLs rewriting rules permission, which the Administrator role has by default.

chapters.title: Redirect a renamed page
chapters.subtitle: Create a Redirect rule and test it

steps.text: Choose Tools, then URL Rewriting. The URL Rewriting Rules page lists the rules of the site, and the list is empty.
Select Add Rule. The Available Rule Types window offers Redirect and Rewrite. Select Add on the Redirect card.
Give the rule the Display Name Redirect about-us to about. In Match URL Pattern, type a caret, then /about-us, then a dollar sign, to match the old address and nothing longer.
Check Case Insensitive, so the pattern ignores letter case and an address typed as /About-Us is caught as well.
Query String Policy controls the part of an address after a question mark. Append Query String from Original Request keeps it, and Exclude Query String from Original Request drops it.
Redirect Type sets the response code. Found (302), the default, is a temporary redirect. Choose Moved Permanently (301) for a page that has moved for good, so bookmarks and links can be updated.
In The Substitution URL Pattern, type /about, the address visitors should reach. Then select Save.
The message reads Rule created successfully, and the list shows one row with the rule name, its source, and when it was created.
Let's visit the old address, /about-us, with a parameter added after a question mark. A green label shows the address we ask for.
The browser follows the redirect and opens the About page. The label shows the address it ended on, /about, with the parameter attached, because the policy appends the query string.

chapters.title: Rewrite an address
chapters.subtitle: Create a Rewrite rule and test it

steps.text: Back on URL Rewriting Rules, select Add Rule. This time, select Add on the Rewrite card.
Name the rule Serve media from img. In Match URL Pattern, type a caret, /img/, parentheses around dot star, and a dollar sign. This matches any address that starts with /img/.
In The Substitution URL Pattern, type /media/ followed by $1. The $1 stands for the text captured after /img/, so /img/photo.jpg is served from /media/photo.jpg.
Check Case Insensitive, and set Query String Policy to Exclude Query String from Original Request, so that parameters on the old address are not passed on.
Check Stop Evaluation of Subsequent Rules. When this rule matches, the rules below it in the list are ignored. Then select Save.
The list shows both rules, with the Redirect rule first and the Rewrite rule below it.
Let's open /img/about-bg.jpg. The site answers with the image stored under /media, and the label shows that the address in the browser did not change.
Each row shows a drag handle, a checkbox, the rule name, its source, and when it was created. Edit changes a rule, and Delete removes it.
Edit opens the same form with the saved values. Select Cancel to leave the rule as it is.
Drag a row by its handle to move the rule up or down. The order of the list is the order in which the rules are checked.
Select Delete on a row, and the Delete window asks you to confirm. Select Ok, and the page confirms that the rule was deleted.
A Redirect rule changes the address, a Rewrite rule keeps it, and the order of the list decides which rule is checked first. Thanks for watching.
